title: Color Changes
description: Switch yarn colors cleanly so stripes and motifs look intentional instead of messy.

content.summary: Learn to finish the final yarn-over of a stitch with a new color and carry on without a bulky jump.
content.whyItMatters: Color changes unlock stripes, granny projects, and decorative details without forcing the user to improvise at the exact moment the pattern gets interesting.
steps: Work the stitch until the last yarn-over is still waiting on the hook.
Drop the old color, pull the new color through to finish the stitch, and tighten both tails gently.
Continue crocheting with the new color and keep the tails out of the working path.
If the pattern is striped, cut and rejoin when the jump would show, or carry the yarn only when it stays hidden.
content.practice: Crochet a short swatch of two rows in one color, then switch colors at the start of the next row and repeat twice.
commonMistakes: Changing colors after finishing the stitch, which creates a visible dot of the old color.
Pulling the first stitch too tight and making the join pucker.
